title: Determination of structural ensembles and correlated dynamics of a multi-domain protein
protocol: Generate stable homodimers by inserting a zipper motif close to the native dimerization site.
Select possible labeling positions in each domain based on conservation among homologues, preferring low-conservation regions.
Choose positions within small loops that are evenly distributed and not located at domain interfaces for labeling.
Create point mutants by site-directed mutagenesis following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Purify plasmid DNA of mutants and verify mutants by sequencing.
Transform plasmid with verified single point mutant gene into bacteria for expression.
Express protein mutants and purify them by chromatography to achieve > 90% purity, as checked by SDS-PAGE.
Prepare samples for dye labeling.
Label cysteine mutants with maleimide dyes.
Add 10 mM TCEP and incubate at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Remove TCEP and change buffer to PBS pH 6.7 using a desalting column.
Concentrate the protein with vivaspin500 centricons if the concentration drops below 30 μM.
Add a two-fold excess of maleimide dye to the protein.
Incubate in the dark for one hour at room temperature.
Remove excess dye and change buffer to measurement buffer using a desalting column.
Exchange one donor with one acceptor labeled mutant in multimeric complexes if needed.
Incubate mixed samples for about 20 minutes at 47°C to accelerate Hsp90 coiled coil zipper opening, if applicable.
Centrifuge extensively at 14000 g for one hour to remove possible aggregates.
Correlate measured FRET efficiencies with stoichiometries in a scatter plot.
Test purified and labeled mutants for their activity compared to the wild-type protein if enzymatic activity is known.
Exclude any labeled mutant that loses its activity completely from further experiments immediately.
Clean glass slides in an ultrasonic bath with 2% Hellmanex for 10 min.
Rinse slides twice in ddH2O in an ultrasonic bath for 10 min each.
Clean slides at 55°C for 2 h in piranha solution.
Rinse slides thoroughly with ddH2O.
Clean glass slides again in an ultrasonic bath with 2% Hellmanex for 10 min.
Clean slides at 55°C for 2 h in RCA solution.
Rinse slides thoroughly with ddH2O.
Put slides in ddH2O in ultrasonic bath.
Storage slides in ddH2O.
Dry slides with compressed pure nitrogen.
Place slides in pure acetone.
Incubate slides for 5-10 min in acetone containing Vectabond.
Swivel slides in ddH2O.
Place each slide on a petri dish.
Apply 70 µL of PEG solution onto each slide.
Cover the PEG solution with an untreated slide.
Keep the setup dark, cold at 4°C and humid with water-soaked wipes.
After 3 hours, swivel slides in ddH2O to wash off unbound PEG.
Dry slides with nitrogen.
Store slides dark, cold ideally in a vacuum chamber.
Cut 5mm-holes into Nescofilm using a laser cutter for 3 rows and 8 columns.
Drill holes into a 1 mm-thick teflon block.
Place the Nescofilm between a functionalized slide and the teflon block.
Burden the chamber on a heat plate at 70°C for 20 minutes with the slide side down.
Reuse the Teflon block after cleaning it with 2% Hellmanex and ddH2O.
Determine the normalized fluorescence spectrum F̅_D(λ) for each donor-labeled mutant.
Record the absorbance spectrum for each acceptor-labeled mutant.
Collect micro- and macro-time data using the described confocal setup to obtain FRET efficiencies, stoichiometries, and time-resolved anisotropies.

For each FRET pair and condition (nucleotide, cofactor, salt concentration), record at least 1000 single molecule events (at least 30 minutes per measurement at a sample concentration of about 50 pM).
Measure each pair under the conditions that shift the equilibrium among state populations.
Start with measuring FRET pairs between two large domains (each with four labeling positions).

Calculate the quantum yield for each donor position from the measured fluorescence lifetime τ_D0 and the given fluorescence lifetime τ'_D0 and quantum yield Q'_D specified by the manufacturer: Q_D = Q'_D * τ_D0 / τ'_D0.
Calculate the overlap integral J(λ) for each FRET pair: J_DA(λ) = ∫ F̅_D(λ) ε_A(λ) λ^4 dλ.
Assume the extinction coefficient in the absorbance spectra maximum remains constant and calculate the extinction spectrum ε_A(λ).
Calculate the Förster radius R_0 for each FRET pair using the determined overlap spectra J and donor quantum yield QD.
Assume κ^2=2/3.
Correct FRET efficiencies for leakage, direct excitation, β- and γ-factors iteratively by checking for self-consistency within the network.
Calculate preliminary distances from corrected efficiencies with a probability distribution analysis.
Compare the data to existing structural data using the FPS tool.
Verify experimental distances against model structures for state assignment.
Assign states during global domain arrangement if no existing global structure is available.
Check the fraction of dark states for donor and acceptor dye with fluorescence correlation spectroscopy.
Use moderate excitation powers to fit the autocorrelation of the donor fluorescence intensity after donor excitation.
Fit the autocorrelation of the acceptor fluorescence intensity after acceptor excitation using macro-time data.
Choose an average laser power of 50 µW, resulting in dark state fractions of less than 3% for Atto550 and Atto647N.

Calculate time-resolved dye anisotropies from parallel and perpendicularly polarized fluorescence intensities N|| and N⊥ using micro-time data after excitation with the linearly polarized donor laser or acceptor laser.
Correct for relative detection efficiencies in the calculation of anisotropy, considering depolarization factors for objectives with high numerical aperture.
Determine the combined anisotropy, if possible for each state separately.
Determine a threshold for the combined anisotropy with distance network.
Apply the threshold value r_C=0.22 to the data set.
Test for state-dependent local conformational changes.
Compare position-specific anisotropies between different states.
Correlate time-resolved anisotropies with accessible volumes calculated using FPS software.
Check for changes in accessible volumes between states.
Use intra-domain and intra-monomer FRET pairs to test for rearrangements within.
Arrange domains with assigned distances for each state.
Calculate mean dye positions from accessible volumes using FPS software.
Generate fluorescence intensity traces with different time bins.
Create efficiency histograms for each time interval.
Run the software tool ‘MDAgenDistances’ to generate distances and their standard deviations of a Gaussian distribution and uncertainties.
Run the software tool ‘MDAgenStructures’ to generate average structures with different chi^2 values.
Generate structures from distance subsets using the software tool ‘MDAgenSubsets’.
If solutions are ambiguous, substitute domain structures with other crystal structures if known.
If ambiguity persists after substitution, return to step \(a) or \(d\) and measure further FRET pairs.
Generate an ensemble of structures using the software tool ‘MDAgenEnsembles’.
Refine the ensemble structures from the domain arrangement with MD simulations.
Screen the results with the FPS software.
In case deviations occur during screening, repeat the global distance distribution analysis and subsequent domain arrangement.
Test the stability and fast local dynamics of the optimal solution with unrestrained MD simulations in explicit solvent.
